props.title: Night of the Living Dead
props.initialSlug: Strangers fight zombies in a farmhouse siege

sections.content: Night of the Living Dead revolutionized horror by injecting raw social commentary into its zombie apocalypse. George Romero shot in stark black-and-white on a shoestring budget, creating a claustrophobic nightmare where the real monsters aren't just the undead - they're human nature itself. The casting of Duane Jones as Ben, a Black protagonist in 1968 America, adds layers of racial tension that culminate in the film's gut-punch ending. This laid groundwork for socially conscious horror like Get Out (2017) and The Babadook (2014).

sections.content: The film's influence extends far beyond horror. Its public domain status meant endless reruns on late-night TV, embedding zombie tropes deep into pop culture. Shaun of the Dead (2004) lovingly satirized these conventions while The Walking Dead (2010-2022) expanded them into long-form television drama. Romero's DIY filmmaking approach inspired generations of independent directors like John Carpenter with Halloween (1978) and Sam Raimi with The Evil Dead (1981).

Modern zombie films continue building on Romero's foundation of social commentary. World War Z (2013) examines global pandemic response, while Warm Bodies (2013) subverts the genre through romance. #Alive (2020) and Host (2020) adapt zombie isolation themes for our social media age. Each iteration reflects contemporary anxieties, just as Romero's original captured late-1960s racial and social upheaval. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Technical Innovation

sections.content: Romero's practical effects, achieved through makeup artist Tom Savini's ingenuity, established zombie visual standards still referenced today. The Return of the Living Dead (1985) added punk rock energy and black humor, while Day of the Dead (1985) pushed practical gore effects to new extremes. Modern films like Army of the Dead (2021) blend practical and digital effects, but Romero's practical approach remains influential in works like The Battery (2012) and One Cut of the Dead (2017).
